sections.heading: Section 1: Exponential Growth and Decay Fundamentals

questions.q: Which function represents exponential decay with an initial value of $450$ and a decay rate of $8\%$ per year?
questions.answer: In exponential decay, the base is $b = 1 - r$. With $r = 0.08$, $b = 1 - 0.08 = 0.92$. The model is $f(t) = 450(0.92)^t$.

questions.q: An exponential function passes through $(0, 6)$ and $(2, 54)$. If $f(x) = a b^x$ where $b > 0$, what is the value of $b$?
If a quantity grows continuously at an annual rate of $5\%$, what is the continuous growth model for an initial investment of 1200 dollars?
questions.answer: Continuous compounding or continuous growth is modeled by $A(t) = P e^{rt}$. Here $P = 1200$ and $r = 0.05$, yielding $A(t) = 1200 e^{0.05t}$.

questions.q: A bacterial culture doubles every 4 hours. If there are initially 500 bacteria, which equation models the population after $t$ hours?
questions.answer: The doubling model is $P(t) = P_0 \cdot 2^{t/d}$, where $d$ is the doubling time. Here $d = 4$, so $P(t) = 500 \cdot 2^{t/4}$.

questions.q: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 15 days. If a sample contains 80 grams initially, how much remains after 45 days?
questions.answer: The number of elapsed half-lives is $\frac{45}{15} = 3$. Remaining amount: $80 \cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = 80 \cdot \frac{1}{8} = 10\text{ g}$.

questions.q: If the doubling time of an investment is 12 years, what is the annual growth factor $b$ in $A(t) = A_0 b^t$?
questions.answer: Doubling time satisfies $b^{12} = 2$. Taking the 12th root yields $b = 2^{1/12} \approx 1.0595$.

questions.q: Rewrite $f(t) = 100(1.21)^{t/2}$ in the form $f(t) = 100 b^t$. What is $b$?
If $P(t) = 250 e^{0.08 t}$, what is the equivalent discrete annual growth factor rounded to four decimal places?
questions.answer: $e^{0.08 t} = (e^{0.08})^t$. Since $e^{0.08} \approx 1.083287$, the annual factor is approximately $1.0833$.

questions.q: A medication decreases in the bloodstream by $30\%$ every 6 hours. By what factor does it decrease per hour?
questions.answer: A decrease of $30\%$ means a 6-hour factor of $1 - 0.30 = 0.70$. The hourly factor $b$ satisfies $b^6 = 0.70 \Rightarrow b = (0.70)^{1/6}$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Comparing Linear and Exponential Growth

questions.q: A linear function $L(x) = 50x + 100$ and an exponential function $E(x) = 2^x$ are compared for large $x > 0$. Which statement is true?
choices: Eventually $E(x) > L(x)$ for all sufficiently large $x$
Eventually $L(x) > E(x)$ because its initial rate of change is 50
They will intersect infinitely many times
$L(x)$ and $E(x)$ grow at the same rate asymptotically
questions.answer: Any exponential growth function with base $b > 1$ will eventually exceed any linear or polynomial function for sufficiently large values of $x$.

questions.q: Which data set represents an exponential function rather than a linear function?
questions.answer: In an exponential function, consecutive $y$-values over equal intervals have a constant ratio: $\frac{18}{6} = 3, \frac{54}{18} = 3, \frac{162}{54} = 3$. This confirms exponential behavior.

questions.q: What is the domain and range of the function $f(x) = 4 - 3(2)^x$?
questions.answer: Exponential functions are defined for all real $x$, so domain is $(-\infty, \infty)$. Since $2^x > 0$ for all $x$, $-3(2)^x < 0$, which makes $4 - 3(2)^x < 4$. The range is $(-\infty, 4)$.
